title: Reduce gdscript VM instruction set and simplify VM code
body:
The VM has, in my opinion, far far too many opcodes, and the code is, frankly, a bit messy and hard to understand to someone unfamiliar trying to work on it (no offense). In the pursuit of easier maintenance and improvement, I have sought to refactor much of the VM code to be easier to read and understand. I am not seeking to change the functionality of the VM in this PR.

I am doing the following:
- Reduce instruction set to 30 opcodes.
- Pull out blocks from their branches of the 3000-line behemoth VM run loop into their own smaller chunks.
- Structure the new functions in a way that they can be pretty easily refactored once other improvements are in place, I.E. unified type representation.
- Improving code clarity by reducing the use of unnecessary macros (such as `DISPATCH_OPCODE` instead of simply `continue`.) This is perhaps controversial and not the C++ way to do things, but I believe macros should be used to reduce repetitive work rather than make a DSL that someone has to learn in order to understand what's going on.
- Slight optimization where the different opcode executions are instead function pointers in an array, instead of a switch statement (preventing lots of branching).
- Documenting the code.

Opcode reduction strategy and rationale:
I noticed most of the opcodes were the same action in a different context. So I simplified by only having the one opcode for the action, and adding an argument to some of the opcodes that further defines which specific context it takes. The argument also carries a flag notifying whether the opcode is "validated" or not.
This may seem like kicking the can down the road, but this is in aim to make it easy to remove this behavior or modify it easily if things change in the future.
The current argument is a single byte formatted as follows:
```
0 | 000_0000
Is Validated? | Sub behavior
``` 
The sub behavior codes are stored in enums in `gdscript_function.h`. Currently the byte is stored as a full int, since each bytecode chunk appears to be an integer. 

This is a work in progress, as cleaning the code is tedious. If there's any changes you would like along the way, let me know. And yes, I'll squash the commits before the PR is actually done.
